subject: Next steps: VPC-hosted inference acceptance criteria & risk log
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Byrne <alex.byrne@medicore.com>, Rachel Gordon <r.gordon@medicore.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: VPC-hosted inference acceptance criteria & risk log

Alex / Rachel — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. I captured the items we discussed around networking, data residency, and the air-gap constraint, plus a short acceptance criteria draft you can react to.

Summary of pain & goals (from today's discovery)
- Primary driver: regulated PHI workflows require customer-managed VPC with no outbound internet egress for certain data sets.
- Goal: host model inference inside Medicore VPC, maintain audit logging, support KMS with customer keys, and meet SOC 2 + regional residency for EU-sourced patients (phase 2).
- Constraint: existing on-prem firewall appliances with strict IP allowlist and no NAT for inference nodes.

Draft acceptance criteria (please flag additions)
1) Network: Configured private endpoint (ENI) that only accepts traffic from Medicore app tier; IP allowlist and explicit port mappings documented.
2) Egress policy: Ability to operate with zero internet egress for production dataset flows; optional outbound channels only for telemetry (with customer opt-in).
3) KMS: Support for customer KMS/HSM integration (AWS KMS key aliases or bring-your-own HSM).
4) Audit & evidence: Delivery of audit logs (token-level and API call traces) for 90 days and SOC 2 artifacts during procurement.
5) Failover: Graceful fallback policy to a dedicated-hosted variant in a separate region if local capacity is exhausted — only if Medicore signs off on cross-region residency rules.

Risk log (initial)
- Risk 1: Network architecture may require on-prem firewall changes that take procurement approval — impact: schedule slip. Owner: Medicore networking.
- Risk 2: KMS/HSM integration timelines unknown — impact: feature gating for encryption-at-rest; Owner: Redwood security (Hannah).
- Risk 3: Zero-egress requirement could block telemetry/metrics collection — mitigation: asynchronous, encrypted blob transfer via signed S3 presigned URLs (customer opt-in). Owner: Marcus.

Proposed next steps and dates
- Redwood to share baseline VPC acceptance checklist and preliminary architecture diagram (attached) — owner: Marcus — ETA: Mon 09/28
- Medicore to confirm any firewall appliance model and allowlist process — owner: Alex — ETA: Wed 09/30
- Redwood security (Hannah) to start KMS questionnaire and list integration options — owner: Hannah — ETA: Fri 10/02
- Schedule technical deep-dive (network & ops) with Medicore infra + Redwood SRE — proposed: week of 10/05.

Attachments: vpc-acceptance-checklist.xlsx (stub), redwood-prelim-arch.png (stub)

If this matches your notes, Alex/Rachel can reply with clarifications and we will convert the acceptance criteria into a short MOP (mutual action plan) + scoping estimate.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Alex Byrne <alex.byrne@medicore.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Rachel Gordon <r.gordon@medicore.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: VPC-hosted inference acceptance criteria & risk log

Marcus — thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our end:

1) KMS/HSM: We will need a BYOK flow; Medicore runs an HSM cluster on-prem. We want the option to keep keys on-prem and never export them. Can you confirm if Redwood supports remote HSM integration (PKCS#11) or if a proxy/KMS bridge is required?

2) Zero egress: The legal team will only allow telemetry if it is optional and goes through an approved S3 bucket in our account. We will not permit any outbound DNS resolution from the inference subnet.

3) Firewall: Our current firewall is a Palo Alto PA-3220, managed by a centralized change window team. Any IP allowlist changes require a 2-week lead time.

If we can get written acceptance criteria that reflect BYOK + zero egress (with the optional telemetry flow), we can move to an NDA + PoC timeline. Also please include an estimate (ballpark will do) for Redwood effort to stand up the VPC integration for a pilot (1 dev/test + 1 prod inference node fleet).

Thanks — I can loop our infra lead into the technical deep-dive once we have the checklist.

—Alex
VP Product, Medicore Health
alex.byrne@medicore.com

On Fri, Sep 25, 2026 at 2:02 PM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com> wrote:
> (quoted call recap)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Byrne <alex.byrne@medicore.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>, Rachel Gordon <r.gordon@medicore.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: VPC-hosted inference acceptance criteria & risk log

Alex — appreciate the specifics. Quick responses and owners from our side: 

- KMS/HSM: Hannah will map the integration options. Short answer: Redwood can support a PKCS#11 bridge or an on-prem HSM proxy in most cases; we'll document the trade-offs. Hannah — can you add a short matrix (BYOK on-prem HSM vs AWS KMS vs Bring-your-HSM) and highlight required connectors? Target: 10/02.

- Telemetry/Egress: We hear you on no DNS/resolution from inference subnets. Our suggestion: operate production inference nodes in strict zero-egress mode; for operational telemetry we can use a customer-approved S3 transfer with signed objects and explicit approvals. Marcus will document the telemetry opt-in flow and required IAM role.

- Timeline & ballpark estimate: For a pilot (1 dev/test, 1 prod fleet) we estimate 3-4 weeks of scoped engineering effort plus one week of joint ops planning. This includes network engineering, KMS integration, and a short security review. We'll capture detailed line items in the MAP doc.

Action items (owners + ETA)
- Redwood: finalize VPC acceptance checklist, include explicit firewall port list, and provide a pilot scoping estimate (Marcus) — ETA: 2026-09-28
- Redwood Security: KMS/HSM options matrix (Hannah) — ETA: 2026-10-02
- Medicore: confirm firewall change window and provide contact for infra lead (Alex) — ETA: 2026-09-30
- Scheduling: Marcus to propose 2 slots for technical deep-dive next week (Marcus) — ETA: 2026-09-28

We will convert these into a short MAP and attach a preliminary Statement of Work for procurement once Medicore confirms pilot scope.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com
